title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from p.651). S is a base scheme, ultimately a trait (spectrum of a DVR) of mixed characteristic, with generic point y of characteristic 0 and closed point s. G is a group scheme over S (affine, e.g. GL_n), and g in G(S) is an element whose generic fibre g_y is unipotent. In characteristic 0 there is a unique one-parameter subgroup phi_y: G_{a,y} -> G_y with phi_y(1) = g_y, given by phi_y(λ) = exp(λ log g_y). By uniqueness there is a largest open set U on which phi extends. After localizing at a maximal point of S \ U, the question becomes: over a trait S, does phi_y extend to a homomorphism f: G_{a,S} -> G with f(1) = g?

This page.
(i) Grothendieck forms L_y = phi_y(G_{a,y}) and its schematic closure L in G. L is a flat, reduced closed subgroup scheme. He then removes the non-neutral components L_{s,i} of the special fibre to get L^0, the neutral-component group scheme. The natural hope is L^0 ≅ G_{a,S}. He immediately notes there is no reason for (L^0)_s = (L_s)^0 to be reduced.
(ii) He observes that L^0 ≅ G_a is not necessary for an extension f to exist. f need not be a monomorphism: f_s could fail to be mono, and could even be trivial when g_s = 1. Even when g_s ≠ 1, it is unclear that phi_s is mono.
(iii) He specializes to G = Aut(M) ≅ GL_n, with M free of rank n. Then phi_y(λ) = Σ X^i λ^i / i! with X = log g_y nilpotent in End_K(M_K), K = k(y). The next page turns this into the integrality question: given that exp(X) and exp(-X) are integral, are all X^i/i! integral for 1 ≤ i ≤ n-1? He then examines n = 4, and shows it is fine when 2 is invertible.

Modern reading: this is the integrality of the exponential/logarithm of unipotent elements over Z_(p). Equivalently: is a unipotent element of G(Z_(p)) contained in the image of a homomorphism G_a -> G defined over Z_(p)? The answer is yes when p is large relative to the nilpotence order (X^p = 0), and no in general.

Concrete check, n = 3, p = 2, A = Z_(2).
- Take g = [[1,1,1],[0,1,1],[0,0,1]], which lies in GL_3(A). Then X = log g = [[0,1,1/2],[0,0,1],[0,0,0]] is not integral.
- phi(λ) has entries λ and λ(λ+1)/2.
- The closure L has coordinate ring A[λ,μ]/(λ^2 + λ - 2μ). Its special fibre is two copies of A^1 (λ = 0 and λ = 1).
- So L^0 is obtained by inverting 1+λ, and L^0 ≅ G_{a,S} with coordinate λ/2 = μ/(1+λ).
- But g lies on the non-neutral component (λ = 1). Hence no f: G_{a,S} -> G with f(1) = g exists.
- Only φ_y∘[2] extends, and that extension is an isomorphism onto L^0.

This illustrates exactly the mechanism Grothendieck's L / L^0 set-up is designed to detect: the obstruction is that g_s lies outside the neutral component of L_s.
errors: No error on this page itself; it is exploratory and Grothendieck flags his own doubts (non-reducedness of (L_s)^0, non-mono f_s).

Related caution for the next page: in the n = 3 case, if X is not assumed integral and 2 is not invertible, the extension can fail. Example over Z_(2): g = [[1,1,1],[0,1,1],[0,0,1]], log g has entry 1/2. Grothendieck's crossing-out of 'aussi' after 'Pour n=3' suggests he noticed n = 3 is not trivial. The analysis of (11) for n = 4 seems to assume X is already integral, an assumption not justified by (9) alone.

ideas.what: Extending the canonical one-parameter subgroup through a unipotent element from the generic fibre (char 0) to a mixed-characteristic trait. Reduction to the local case via a maximal open set of extension plus uniqueness.
ideas.modern_name: Integral exponentiation of unipotent elements / saturation over Z_(p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (saturation, Moursund lectures 1998; semisimplicity of tensor products), Nori 1987, Seitz 2000, Deligne 2014, Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran 2017
ideas.where_published: Not known in published Grothendieck texts; SGA3 treats closely related closure / neutral-component issues

ideas.what: Schematic closure L of the generic one-parameter subgroup, and its neutral component L^0 (removing non-neutral components of the special fibre); worry that (L_s)^0 may be non-reduced.
ideas.modern_name: Flat closure of a subgroup in a model; identity component of a flat group scheme over a DVR; Néron-type smoothening
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA3 (Demazure–Grothendieck); Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models; Waterhouse–Weisfeiler on models of G_a
ideas.where_published: SGA3 (closure and neutral component of group schemes over a base)

ideas.what: Reduction for GL_n: the extension exists iff X^i/i! is integral for all i < n, given that exp(±X) are integral.
ideas.modern_name: Integrality of truncated exponential / divided powers of nilpotent matrices
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Serre for the bound p ≥ nilpotence order

missed.claim: Grothendieck's framework (closure L, neutral component L^0, possible non-mono f_s) anticipates the later theory of saturation and integral exponentials of unipotent elements over Z_(p) (Serre, Seitz, McNinch, Deligne, Balaji–Deligne–Parameswaran). The non-existence of the extension corresponds exactly to g_s lying outside the neutral component of the special fibre of the closure. This geometric formulation of the obstruction is natural but not the usual way the literature phrases it.
missed.quote: Soit L^0 = L \ (∪ L_{s,i}) ... ses composantes neutres ... prouver que L^0 ≃ G_{a,S}. En fait, je ne vois pas de raison pour que (L^0)_s ... soit réduit!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: a historical precursor showing Grothendieck working on integral one-parameter subgroups, probably for integral or unipotent completions in the Longue Marche context. The mathematics itself is now well understood.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but exploratory treatment of a known question (integrality of exponentials of unipotent elements in mixed characteristic). The L / L^0 set-up is natural and the answer (no, in general, for small p) is standard. Interesting mainly as historical evidence of Grothendieck considering this issue in the Longue Marche sequel.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 is barely legible; reading it as 'sans doute qui sont éliminables en général' (rather than 'si on sont éliminées') is plausible but uncertain.
'On a [?] ... prouver' likely reads 'On a envie de prouver' or 'On aimerait prouver'.

'que f_s ne soit pas mono-mono' is a line-break artefact. The manuscript reads roughly 'il est possible que f ne soit pas mono, i.e. que φ_s ne soit pas mono'; the duplicated clause in the transcription should be merged.
In (6), 'Aut_{O_S}(M) ≃ GL(n)_S' looks right; the subscript is written under 'Aut'.
